parts.text:
Describe the features of the snapshot method and outline how it was used in the Nelson
study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Design an alternative way to investigate moral understanding using the longitudinal method
and describe how it could be conducted.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Evaluate this alternative way of studying moral understanding in practical and ethical terms.

text: Nelson used the snapshot method to investigate children’s moral understanding. An alternative
way to investigate moral understanding would be to use the longitudinal method.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: What is meant by the term ‘generalisations’ in psychology?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why one generalisation can be made from the Milgram study.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of making generalisations from the study by Milgram.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss the extent to which the findings of the Milgram study can be applied to everyday life.

Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question from this section.

text: Milgram conducted a study to investigate obedience.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the ‘cognitive approach’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test)
Loftus and Pickrell (false memories)
Held and Hein (kitten carousel)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how cognitive processes were investigated in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: What problems may psychologists have when they investigate cognitive processes?

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by ‘ecological validity’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Rosenhan (sane in insane places)
Freud (little Hans)
Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how each of these studies has high ecological validity.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
What problems may psychologists have when they try to make their studies ecologically
valid?
